name: Euro-area economy
summary: Euro-area composite PMI slipped to a four-month low of 51.7 in October, still above 50
state: The final HCOB euro-area composite PMI for October, released on 4 Nov, was 51.7, down from 53.1 in September and a four-month low (Borsa Italiana). Inflation rose to 4.0% in October, a three-year high, as energy costs climbed (Trading Economics). Growth is slowing, but the PMI remains above 50 and no stagnation in GDP has been reported as of 7 Nov, so Normal holds.
for_you: Slower growth tends to show up first in weaker hiring and business investment.
rubric_hit: Composite PMI 51.7 > 50 and GDP positive = Normal

sources.title: Borsa Italiana — Unione Europea, PMI composito in ottobre
Trading Economics — Eurozone inflation hits fresh three-year high

why: The euro area is the UK's largest trading partner; stagnation there hits UK exports and European markets.
drivers: Energy prices, German industry, ECB policy, fiscal rules, China demand.

rubric.alert: Technical recession, or PMI < 45, or bond-spread fragmentation forcing ECB action.
rubric.normal: Positive GDP growth and composite PMI > 50.
